title: A simple laboratory rearing method for chalcid wasps
author: Lilian P Matallana Ramirez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb3riqm6

steps.title: Prepare experimental units
steps.instruction: Puncture air‑exchange holes into each 10 cm × 14 cm clear plastic sealable bag using dissecting needles; place 80–100 Fraser fir seeds into each bag; optionally add soil media or substrate to simulate natural conditions (not required for M. specularis or its parasitoid Mesopolobus).

steps.title: Hang bags on rack
steps.instruction: Attach each prepared bag (experimental unit) to a metal rack with small binder clips, creating a rearing mounting.

steps.title: Set up constant‑temp & photoperiod
steps.instruction: Position the rack in a room kept at 22 ± 2 °C, next to a window, and place the bags 11 cm beneath 1–2 T5‑54 W fluorescent lamps; connect the lamps to a timer programmed to turn on at sunrise and off at sunset, thereby reproducing the natural photoperiod.

steps.title: Set up cold‑dark condition
steps.instruction: Place the rack (with bags) inside a controlled‑environment chamber set to 6 ± 2 °C and complete darkness.

steps.title: Collect insects regularly
steps.instruction: Unclip bags from the rack at least three times each week, examine them to characterize and capture adult insects; note that females and males of M. specularis become trapped at the top of the sealable bag.
